Glenn Lazarus by leave—I move amendments (1) to (3) on sheet 7625: (1) Clause 8, page 8 (line 4), after "wage", insert ", indexed in accordance with the method in section 8A". (2) Clause 8, page 8 (lines 15 to 22), omit subclause (5), substitute: (5) In this Act: _ actual wage_ means the total wages, worked out in accordance with the rules, that a person was paid in respect of all eligible days for the person. _ productivity_ _-scored wage_ means the total wages, worked out in accordance with the rules, that the person could reasonably have been expected to have been paid in respect of all eligible days for the person if the productivity component of a BSWAT assessment had comprised the whole of the BSWAT assessment. (3) Page 8 (after line 22), after clause 8, insert: 8A Indexation (1) This is how to index the excess of a productivity-scored wage over an actual wage for the purposes of paragraph 8(3)(a): _Method statement_ Step 1. Work out how much of the excess is attributable to wages in respect of eligible days for the person concerned in each financial year. Each such amount is the _annual portion_ for the financial year. Step 2. Multiply the oldest annual portion by the indexation factor specified in subsection (2) for the financial year to which that portion is attributable. If the result is not an amount of whole dollars, round the result up to the nearest whole dollar. Step 3. Take the result of step 2. Add to it any annual portion for the next financial year (unless it is the 2014-2015 financial year, in which case go to step 4). Introduced a companion bill making consequential amendments so payments under the new disability wage assessment scheme are eligible for the lump sum tax offset and are not means-tested against income support payments.

Argued that Labor supports the Business Services Wage Assessment Tool Payment Scheme Bill to help around 20,000 workers across almost 200 disability enterprises, welcomed the top-up payment scheme starting 1 July 2014, and criticised the government's scrapping of the Disability Discrimination Commissioner role held by Graeme Innes.

Argued in support of the Business Services Wage Assessment Tool Payment Scheme Bill, describing a 2012 Federal Court finding of indirect discrimination against intellectually disabled workers, and highlighted the Intellectual Disability Foundation of St George in his Barton electorate as part of the roughly 20,000-worker sector the scheme protects.

Argued that Labor supports the payment scheme bill for the almost 200 Australian disability enterprises supporting around 20,000 workers, noted the scheme will remain open until 15 November 2015, and urged wide consultation on a new wage assessment tool to replace the Business Services Wage Assessment Tool developed in 2003.

Argued the bill is designed to derail a class action by up to 10,000 disability enterprise workers seeking fair pay after Mr Nojin and Mr Prior won a Federal Court ruling, noting Mr Nojin had been paid $1.85 an hour, and warned the scheme would cut affected workers' compensation by about half.
